**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat interrupted deployments as unverified**

When an update is interrupted after `ExactReleaseDeploymentCoordinator` transitions the record to `deploying`, the previous `activeRelease` and verified public read-back remain persisted even though the server may already be partially mutated. This branch therefore labels that recovery state “Public site is online and verified” and says no action is required, contradicting the interrupted-deployment recovery action rendered below. Handle `deploying` before this branch, or restrict this verified status to stable `healthy`/`rollback-available` states.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed. `deploying` is now handled before any stable public-verification branch and presents an explicit incomplete/recovery status. The verified human status is additionally restricted to stable `healthy` / `rollback-available` states. This preserves the persisted technical proof as evidence while preventing an interrupted deployment from being presented as currently verified.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop labeling stale active releases as online**

When an update is interrupted after mutating the server but before successful read-back, `activeRelease` still contains the last confirmed release even though the server may now be serving partially updated or different content. The new `deploying` status branch fixes the headline, but this unconditional block still presents that stale release as “Website Release online,” contradicting the incomplete status and potentially misleading recovery decisions. Restrict this label to stable verified states, or describe it as the last confirmed release during `deploying`/`degraded` recovery.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed. The ordinary Release label is now state-aware. Only a stable `healthy` / `rollback-available` deployment with verified public read-back says **Public site is serving**. `deploying`, `degraded`, and `unreachable` states instead say **Last confirmed deployed Website Release**, so persisted `activeRelease` evidence cannot be mistaken for current public truth during recovery. Added a regression that requires the recovery label and forbids `Public site is serving` for an interrupted deployment.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Surface known public read-back mismatches**

When `verifyPublicHttps` records `publicReadBack.state === 'mismatch'` while the deployment remains `healthy` or `rollback-available`, this generic branch describes verification as merely incomplete and tells the owner to complete it, even though HiVenues already knows the public endpoint is serving the wrong identity or Release. Add a mismatch-specific human status before this fallback so the leading lifecycle summary exposes the failure rather than leaving it to the lower diagnostic card.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed. A known `publicReadBack.state === 'mismatch'` on a stable `healthy` / `rollback-available` deployment now gets an explicit leading status: **Public site does not match this deployment**. The summary explains that the exact runtime or Website Release identity did not match and directs the owner to the mismatch diagnostics before another public change. A regression now requires that failure summary and forbids verified/serving language and the public-site shortcut for this state.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Populate mismatch fields in the new fixture**

This fixture reaches the existing mismatch diagnostic, which unconditionally evaluates `deployment.publicEndpoint.publicReadBack.mismatchFields.join(', ')`; because `mismatchFields` is absent here, the new test throws a `TypeError` during EJS rendering before any of its assertions run, failing the test suite whenever dependencies are installed. Add a representative `mismatchFields` array to the fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't call an unverified server release public**

When the selected Release matches `activeRelease` but the deployment has no verified public read-back—for example, an established server before a domain is connected—`sameWebsiteRelease` is still true and this review says the Release is already “public content.” An active Release only proves what is installed on the server, so this reintroduces the exact server-versus-public-site ambiguity the lifecycle UI is intended to remove; describe it as already deployed content or gate the public wording on verified public proof.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat interrupted deployments as unverified**

When an update is interrupted after `ExactReleaseDeploymentCoordinator` transitions the record to `deploying`, the previous `activeRelease` and verified public read-back remain persisted even though the server may already be partially mutated. This branch therefore labels that recovery state “Public site is online and verified” and says no action is required, contradicting the interrupted-deployment recovery action rendered below. Handle `deploying` before this branch, or restrict this verified status to stable `healthy`/`rollback-available` states.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed. `deploying` is now handled before any stable public-verification branch and presents an explicit incomplete/recovery status. The verified human status is additionally restricted to stable `healthy` / `rollback-available` states. This preserves the persisted technical proof as evidence while preventing an interrupted deployment from being presented as currently verified.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop labeling stale active releases as online**

When an update is interrupted after mutating the server but before successful read-back, `activeRelease` still contains the last confirmed release even though the server may now be serving partially updated or different content. The new `deploying` status branch fixes the headline, but this unconditional block still presents that stale release as “Website Release online,” contradicting the incomplete status and potentially misleading recovery decisions. Restrict this label to stable verified states, or describe it as the last confirmed release during `deploying`/`degraded` recovery.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed. The ordinary Release label is now state-aware. Only a stable `healthy` / `rollback-available` deployment with verified public read-back says **Public site is serving**. `deploying`, `degraded`, and `unreachable` states instead say **Last confirmed deployed Website Release**, so persisted `activeRelease` evidence cannot be mistaken for current public truth during recovery. Added a regression that requires the recovery label and forbids `Public site is serving` for an interrupted deployment.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Surface known public read-back mismatches**

When `verifyPublicHttps` records `publicReadBack.state === 'mismatch'` while the deployment remains `healthy` or `rollback-available`, this generic branch describes verification as merely incomplete and tells the owner to complete it, even though HiVenues already knows the public endpoint is serving the wrong identity or Release. Add a mismatch-specific human status before this fallback so the leading lifecycle summary exposes the failure rather than leaving it to the lower diagnostic card.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed. A known `publicReadBack.state === 'mismatch'` on a stable `healthy` / `rollback-available` deployment now gets an explicit leading status: **Public site does not match this deployment**. The summary explains that the exact runtime or Website Release identity did not match and directs the owner to the mismatch diagnostics before another public change. A regression now requires that failure summary and forbids verified/serving language and the public-site shortcut for this state.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Populate mismatch fields in the new fixture**

This fixture reaches the existing mismatch diagnostic, which unconditionally evaluates `deployment.publicEndpoint.publicReadBack.mismatchFields.join(', ')`; because `mismatchFields` is absent here, the new test throws a `TypeError` during EJS rendering before any of its assertions run, failing the test suite whenever dependencies are installed. Add a representative `mismatchFields` array to the fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed. The presentation fixture now supplies representative canonical mismatch evidence with `mismatchFields: ['deployment.releaseId']`. I did not weaken the existing diagnostic to tolerate structurally invalid persisted state.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't call an unverified server release public**

When the selected Release matches `activeRelease` but the deployment has no verified public read-back—for example, an established server before a domain is connected—`sameWebsiteRelease` is still true and this review says the Release is already “public content.” An active Release only proves what is installed on the server, so this reintroduces the exact server-versus-public-site ambiguity the lifecycle UI is intended to remove; describe it as already deployed content or gate the public wording on verified public proof.
